report.answer_text:
A tower crane is made of several main parts. Each has its own job.
Structural parts
Base (foundation)
It is a concrete slab, sometimes with anchor bolts or a fixed cross-frame.
It carries the crane's weight and load, and it keeps the crane stable.
Mast (tower)
It is a lattice steel column built from bolted sections.
It gives the crane its height. Sections can be added so the crane can "climb" as the building grows.
Slewing unit (slewing ring and motor)
It sits at the top of the mast.
It lets the jib, counter-jib, and cab rotate through 360°.
Operator's cab
This is where the operator sits and works the controls.
It is usually mounted beside or just below the slewing unit, which gives a view of the work area.
Jib (working arm)
This is the long horizontal arm that reaches out over the work area.
It carries the trolley and the hoisted load.
Counter-jib (machinery arm)
This is the short arm on the opposite side of the jib.
It holds the counterweights, the hoist motor, and the electrical controls.
Counterweights
These are concrete or steel blocks on the counter-jib.
They balance the load on the jib and stop the crane from tipping.
Tower head / apex (cat head)
This is the peak above the jib and counter-jib.
It supports the pendant (tie) bars that hold up the jib and counter-jib.
Pendant bars (tie rods)
These are cables or rigid bars that run from the apex to the jib and counter-jib.
They carry part of the load to the tower and stiffen the arms.
Lifting parts
Trolley
It runs along the jib, in and out.
It changes the horizontal reach, which is the working radius.
Hoist rope (wire rope) and hoist winch
The winch drum is on the counter-jib. It winds the rope in and out to raise and lower loads.
Hook block (hook and pulley assembly)
It hangs from the trolley and holds the load.
It often has a safety latch.
Support and safety parts
Climbing frame (climbing cage)
It is a hydraulic frame near the top of the mast.
It lifts the upper crane so new mast sections can be inserted. This is called "telescoping."
Ties / anchors (tie-in collars)
Tall cranes are tied to the building at set intervals.
This gives extra stability against wind and load.
Limit switches and load moment indicators
These are safety devices. They limit hoist height, trolley travel, and slewing.
They also stop the crane from lifting more than its rated capacity at a given radius.
Anemometer
It measures wind speed, so work can stop when conditions are unsafe.
Ladders, platforms, and handrails
They give maintenance workers and operators access to the crane.
How they work together
1. The hoist lifts the load.
2. The trolley sets how far out the load is.
3. The slewing unit swings it to the right place.
4. The counterweights and mast keep the crane balanced and stable throughout.
I can go into more detail on any part, such as climbing procedures, load charts, or the types of tower crane (hammerhead, luffing jib, flat-top, self-erecting).
